description: New public changes about Robinhood Chain tokens since your last call, from a watcher that reads public sources on a schedule, from every 15 seconds for the chain and every minute for most exchanges to every 30 minutes for CoinGecko, and keeps each change it sees as an event. The kinds: `pool.created`, a new Uniswap pool for a token that already has a public trace, paired with ETH, WETH, USDG or another such token; `maker.approval` and `maker.receipt`, the first approval or first receipt of a token by a wallet brainchain_market_maker_holdings follows; `maker.pool_queued`, a market maker adding one of a token's pools to its trading contracts' approved list for the first time: Wintermute's multisig queues each pool on its role registry, and the pool can be traded once the role takes effect, hours or days later; `bitgo.pr_opened`, `bitgo.merged` and `bitgo.released`, a pull request opened in BitGo's public code that adds a Robinhood Chain token, its merge into master, and the first release of BitGo's @bitgo/statics package that includes the token; `trustwallet.pr_opened`, `trustwallet.merged`, `metamask.pr_opened` and `metamask.merged`, the same for Trust Wallet's and MetaMask's token lists; `robinhood.pair_added` and `robinhood.tradability_changed`, a symbol entering the pair list Robinhood serves to API clients, with `pairsRead`, the number of pairs read, and its tradability changing there; that list leaves out most price-only pairs, so a symbol can have had a price on Robinhood before it enters the list. `robinhood.page_added` is a page in Robinhood's crypto sitemap, which has the price-only pairs too; `kucoin.listed`, `gate.listed`, `lifi.listed` and `coingecko.listed`, a token's contract appearing on those lists; `venue.listed`, an exchange adding its first spot or perpetual market for a token, read from the market lists Binance Futures, Upbit, Bithumb and Bitget publish, with the market, its `status` (pre-trading, auction, trading or halted) and the time the exchange gives it, where it gives one; `venue.status_changed`, that market's status changing, such as from its opening auction to trading; and `venue.announced`, an exchange's announcement naming a token: Kraken's Asset Listings posts, Bithumb's market-added notices and Bitget's coin-listing announcements. An exchange's entry is tied to a token by the contract the exchange gives, or else by its own name for the asset, and `detail.match` says which; one with neither rests on the symbol alone and is marked `unconfirmed`. Each event has `id`; `kind`; `token`, with `address`, `symbol` and `name`, any of which can be null, since Robinhood names a token by symbol only; `source`; `ref`, a link, transaction or commit to check it by; `at`, when the source dates the change, or null for a source that publishes no date; `observedAt`, when the watcher saw it; `detail`; and `context`. `context.worth` is the token's market cap, price and deepest pool's depth within 2% of its price (`depth2pctUsd`) when the event went out, or null with `worthMissing` saying why; `context.priorTraces` lists the token's dated public steps before the event, as brainchain_token_timeline reads them, and `context.priorEvents` what the watcher had already recorded for the token. `context.counts` says how often earlier tokens with the step the event records were listed within 7, 30 and 90 days, from the newest BrainChain MCP dataset, as brainchain_trace_outcomes counts them: what happened to earlier tokens, which says nothing of this one. An event goes out at most 10 seconds after the watcher sees it, with the context ready by then: `context.pending` names what is still being read, and the event is filled in once it is, so read it again by its `id` to see the rest. For a token named only by symbol, `context.matches` lists the Robinhood Chain tokens the watcher knows by that symbol: two tokens can share one, so compare names before reading it as the same token. Pass the `next` of your previous answer as `since` to get only what is new; `since` also takes a time in ISO 8601, for what the watcher saw from then on. Without `since` you get the newest events. `kinds` keeps some kinds, or every kind from one source, such as `bitgo`; `tokens` keeps some tokens, by contract address, symbol or BitGo id; `limit` caps the answer at 1 to 1,000 events, 100 by default, and `more` says whether more matched. An event says what became public and when. It does not say why, and most tokens with these traces are never listed. The changes come from BrainChain's watcher at https://watch.usebrainchain.com, or from your own `brainchain-mcp watch --serve` when BRAINCHAIN_WATCH_URL names it. What was already public when the watcher first started is its baseline, which it never reports as new. To have changes sent to you as they happen, use brainchain_watch. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

kinds.description: Optional: kinds to keep, such as bitgo.pr_opened, or a source's prefix, such as bitgo.

limit.description: Optional: at most this many events, from 1 to 1000. 100 by default.

since.description: Optional: the `next` of an earlier answer, for the events after it, or a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-11-19T00:00:00Z.

tokens.description: Optional: tokens to keep, by contract address, symbol or BitGo id.
